html:
The return of Jewish exiles from Babylon to Judah after the Persian king Cyrus the Great allowed it in 538 BCE, as told in the biblical books of Ezra and Nehemiah. It ended the exile that began when Babylon destroyed Jerusalem in 586 BCE.

Groups went back in waves, led by figures such as Zerubbabel, a descendant of the old kings, and the high priest Joshua. They rebuilt the Temple, the Second Temple, completing it around 516 or 515 BCE under Darius the Great. In the next century the scribe Ezra brought the law of Moses to the forefront, and the governor Nehemiah rebuilt the city walls.

Many Jews chose to stay in Babylon, where a large community lived on until the 20th century. Judah became Yehud, a small province of the Achaemenid Empire. The return opened the Second Temple period, which lasted until the Romans destroyed the Temple in 70 CE.
